candidates.statement: The stakeholder uses the social network web application daily for news browsing, occasional job-posting search and general scrolling for daily information.
candidates.modality: descriptive present-tense usage ('I daily use ...', 'sometimes')

evidence_candidates.quote: So I daily use social network web application for like news browsing.
And sometimes I search for job posting information.

candidates.statement: The stakeholder does not want to miss any important information, such as major events happening internationally.
candidates.modality: explicit avoidance ('I do not want to miss out')

evidence_candidates.quote: I do not want to miss out any important information like if there are any great events going on internationally.

candidates.statement: New job postings count as the kind of important information the stakeholder does not want to miss.
candidates.modality: explicit avoidance, example given under the same 'do not want to miss out' clause

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe there are some new job posting

candidates.statement: The AI recommendation algorithm should record the stakeholder's likes and comments and recommend content based on his taste; the stakeholder calls it a necessary feature for social applications.
candidates.modality: explicit preference plus necessity claim ('this is the necessary feature')

evidence_candidates.quote: will be fed with my own favorites like when I click likes, and when I comment on the postings of applications
they will record my actions, and after that they will do more like recommendations based on my. on my taste.
I think this is the necessary feature for social applications.

candidates.statement: To find information the stakeholder scrolls the main feed up and down to locate intended postings.
candidates.modality: description of an action currently taken (answer to 'describe the main action')

evidence_candidates.quote: I can just scroll up and down to to try to locate my intended postings

candidates.statement: To find information the stakeholder opens the daily news ranking and selects the specific news he wants.
candidates.modality: description of an action currently taken

evidence_candidates.quote: I can go into the ranking of the news and select the specific news I want

candidates.statement: The stakeholder uses the search bar, types whatever he wants to search and receives results.
candidates.modality: description of a feature currently used ('I can just click the search bar')

evidence_candidates.quote: I can just click the search bar and type in whatever I want to search

candidates.statement: Search results are returned randomly, so there is no way to get information and results for a specific region, which the stakeholder reports as a problem.
candidates.modality: reported problem ('I think it's kind of a problem for me')

evidence_candidates.quote: There is no way for me to get the get the information and results for that specific region.
because they just give return back the results very randomly

candidates.statement: The stakeholder wants a specific button or feature in the application that lets him search within a specific region such as the city.
candidates.modality: explicit preference ('it would be better for me if ...')

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be better for for me if there is a specific specific button, or or some feature in the application that I could search in a specific region like the city

candidates.statement: The stakeholder agrees to adding limitations or conditions to searching.
candidates.modality: explicit agreement ('Yeah, yeah, yeah.') to the interviewer's restatement

evidence_candidates.quote: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

candidates.statement: Job listing search has fewer problems than housing rental search because AI recommendations push the right postings; housing rental search filters out many useful postings for lack of region narrowing.
candidates.modality: comparative observation, no separate request

evidence_candidates.quote: because it can push you the right postings with artificial intelligence, recommendations.
they will filter out a lot of useful postings

candidates.statement: When looking at a job the stakeholder wants to see how many people are already in the hiring process, to judge whether the company is hiring in large numbers.
candidates.modality: explicit desire ('I might want to see')

evidence_candidates.quote: how how many people are already entering the hiring process
see if this company is on a great number of hiring or not

candidates.statement: The stakeholder wants feedback from people who recently interviewed at the company, to judge whether the company has a high benchmark to pass the interview.
candidates.modality: explicit desire ('I'll get feedback from the interviewees')

evidence_candidates.quote: I'll get feedback from the interviewees who just recently has taken the interviews from the company
does it have a high benchmark to to pass the interview or not

candidates.statement: The stakeholder reports the general job-search experience as good.
candidates.modality: satisfaction statement, no change requested

evidence_candidates.quote: I think the general experience is good for me.

candidates.statement: The stakeholder wants a feature that splits entertainment content from useful content, so that entertainment content is filtered out when he does not want to see it.
candidates.modality: explicit preference ('it would be better if it can have a feature')

evidence_candidates.quote: I think that it would be better if it it can have a feature that you can split the entertainment contents from useful contents
when sometimes I don't wanna see those entertainment contents

candidates.statement: The stakeholder also uses the application for entertainment content such as daily jokes pushed to him.
candidates.modality: soft addition ('maybe some like entertainment stuff')

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, maybe some like entertainment stuff like they will just push you some daily jokes for you.

candidates.statement: Entertainment content arrives as photos and texts on this application, while other platforms such as TikTok use video.
candidates.modality: format description in answer to the interviewer's format question

evidence_candidates.quote: it will be in a form of photos and texts

candidates.statement: The AI recommendation deduces the stakeholder's browsing taste from his history and continuously pushes the latest information that fits that taste.
candidates.modality: explicit account of the benefit ('It's helpful because ...')

evidence_candidates.quote: They can tell. Tell it from your browsing histories.
they will give you the the latest information. That fits your taste continuously.

candidates.statement: The stakeholder knows his data has been leaked and sold or shared by many apps, considers it risky but unavoidable, and has got used to accepting it.
candidates.modality: acceptance of an existing condition ('I just got used to it')

evidence_candidates.quote: I think I know that my data has been leaked before, and it's quite quite risky.
I think that I just accept the the thing that my data will be leaked.

candidates.statement: If he found real damage from a data leak the stakeholder would take lawsuit action.
candidates.modality: conditional personal reaction ('once I found that I will ... take the lawsuit actions')

evidence_candidates.quote: once I found that I will like. take the lawsuit actions

candidates.statement: The stakeholder says he is good with the data-leak situation and does not care much about it.
candidates.modality: indifference statement ('I'm good with it', 'Don't care much about it')

evidence_candidates.quote: I think I'm good with it.
Don't care much about it.

candidates.statement: If the company wanted to address the data issue, it might improve its management so that it does not sell data to other parties.
candidates.modality: hedged proposal ('They might just improve their management')

evidence_candidates.quote: They might just improve their management to ensure that they won't sell data to other parties.

candidates.statement: The stakeholder cannot say which in-application features could protect privacy, and considers data reading for better user experience unavoidable.
candidates.modality: explicit inability to answer ('it's hard to tell')

evidence_candidates.quote: I think it's hard to tell
I think it's unavoidable.

candidates.statement: Social application platforms should strengthen their efforts to handle matrix accounts, which post the same marketing content and flood the feed with irrelevant content that interferes with user experience.
candidates.modality: should-level requirement ('should strengthen their efforts')

evidence_candidates.quote: I think that the social application platforms should strengthen their efforts to handle with matrix accounts.
they just flood the feed with irrelevant contents, and it interferes with user experience.
